Artificial Coral Reefs: The New Rainforests of the Sea
Coral reefs are an important part of the ocean.
They are often called
the rainforests of the sea because many types of marine animals live there.
However, some coral reefs are starting to disappear because of the effects of
climate change, like warmer water and more powerful typhoons.
As a result,
the number of marine animals has been decreasing・Furthermore, the loss
of natural coral reefs can trigger changes in geographical features, and it can
threaten the ecosystem of seashore areas.
To address this problem, scientists
are working on ways to make artificial coral reefs that are strong and safe for
the environment.
Coral reefs are living things.
They form in warm, clear water when
small sea animals called corals attach to hard surfaces in the ocean.
As they
reproduce, they become a larger structure called a reef.
In some places, people
are building artificial coral reefs to protect marine life and beaches.
To build
them, objects are placed in the water for corals and other sea creatures to live
on･
One benefit of artificial coral reefs is that thev can helD Drevent erosion.
Erosion happens when wind and water wear away soil and rock.
For example,
storms reduced the size of a beach in Australia by as much as 30 meters.
People in this area wanted to build a seawall to protect the beach.
However,
seawalls can harm the environment.
Instead, they built an artificial reef using
steel cages filled with rocks and shells.
They put the reef lOO meters from
the shore to make the waves weaker befOre they reach the beach・Incredibly,
in just five years, the beaches stopped eroding and even grew by about 40
meters in some places.
Moreover, it consequently served as a place for marine
creatures or sea weeds to inhabit like a real coral reef.
Another benefit of artificial coral reefs
is that they can help increase
the variety of fish in an area.
Scientists studying one
artificial reef in the
Mediterranean Sea found more than 60 different types of fish living there.

does not take long fOr fish to move in.
In fact, it can take less than six months
for the first animals to make an artificial reef their home.
Artificial coral reefs not only help the environment but can also be good
for business.
They support environmentally friendly travel, or ecotourism.
For example, tourists can explore artificial coral reefs made from different
materia1s.
While crowds of tourists can harm natural coral reefs, artificial ones
are less likely to be damaged.
They also give tourists a new place to explore.
This reduces the pressure on natural coral reefs, giving them time to recover
and grow・Artificial coral reefs can also be built in places that are easier to
re ach・This helps attract more tourists.
While
artificial coral reefs have benefits, there are some problems.
Although they give fish more places to live, fish populations do not always
grow.
Since the public knows where these artificial reefs are, it is easy for
fishers to find and catch many fish, which can hurt fish populations.
Another problem with artificial coral reefs is that only certain materials
can be used to make them.
The materials must be suitable for sea animals
to attach to and strong enough to last in the ocean over time.
Building them
incorrectly can lead to problems. One famous example of a failed artificial reef
is the Osborne Reef, built in the l970s near Florida, in the United States.
The
local government approved the use of two million old tires.
However, over
time, the materials holding the tires together broke down and some of the
tires began to move freely in the ocean.
For this reason, sea animals could not
attach themselves to the material for long, and as a result, these tires became
waste in the ocean and ended up harming sea life.
TherefOre, using the right
materials for artificial coral reefs is important.
Plastic can be harmful to sea
life, and wood does not last long enough・Safe and sustainable materials, such
as ceramics, can be used; actually, there is a 3D-printed artificial coral reef in
the lndian Ocean.
Organic substances can also be usefu1.
Potato starch from
industrial waste is being used to create artificial coral reefs in some areas.
Although there
is
still much work to be done to stop the effects of
climate change on our oceans, people are developing innovative solutions.
The important thing to remember, however, is that these solutions must be
carefully considered before being implemented.
－⑥－27－
